dsa_patterns.title: LRU Cache (Least Recently Used)
bullets: Core Pattern: Doubly Linked List + Hash Map (HashMap maps keys to DLL Nodes for O(1) lookup & eviction).
Complexity: Get: O(1) time | Put: O(1) time | Space: O(Capacity) memory overhead.
Edge Cases: Node update moves to head | Capacity overflow evicts tail prev | Duplicate keys overwrite existing node value.

keywords: find two numbers that add up to
dsa_patterns.title: Two Sum & Three Sum (Hash Map / Two Pointers)
bullets: Core Pattern: Single-pass Hash Map storing complement (target - current_val -> index). For 3Sum: Sort array, fix first element, use Two Pointers for remainder.
Complexity: Two Sum: O(N) time & O(N) space | 3Sum: O(N^2) time & O(1) space.
Edge Cases: Duplicate triplet avoidance (skip adjacent equal values) | Negative numbers and zero handling.

dsa_patterns.title: Sliding Window Maximum (Monotonic Deque)
bullets: Core Pattern: Decreasing Monotonic Deque storing indices of elements. Pop smaller elements from back before inserting.
Complexity: Time: O(N) amortized (each element pushed and popped at most once) | Space: O(K) deque window size.
Edge Cases: Evict indices out of current window [i - k + 1] | Initial window ramp-up.

dsa_patterns.title: Top K Frequent Elements (Bucket Sort / Min-Heap)
bullets: Core Pattern: Count frequencies in Map, then use Bucket Sort array where index = frequency (or Min-Heap of size K).
Complexity: Bucket Sort: O(N) time & O(N) space | Min-Heap: O(N log K) time & O(N) space.
Edge Cases: K equals number of unique elements | All elements have identical frequency.

dsa_patterns.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals (Interval Scheduling)
bullets: Core Pattern: Sort intervals by start time; iterate and merge if current.start <= previous.end by taking max(previous.end, current.end).
Complexity: Time: O(N log N) dominated by sorting | Space: O(N) or O(1) in-place.
Edge Cases: Single interval | Completely nested intervals [1, 10] and [2, 5] | Disjoint intervals.

dsa_patterns.title: Course Schedule (Topological Sort / Kahn's Algorithm)
bullets: Core Pattern: Directed Graph in-degree array + Queue (Kahn's BFS) or 3-color DFS (White/Gray/Black) cycle detection.
Complexity: Time: O(V + E) vertices + edges | Space: O(V + E) adjacency list & in-degree tracker.
Edge Cases: Disconnected graph components | Self-dependency loops (Course A requires Course A).

dsa_patterns.title: Coin Change (Bottom-Up Dynamic Programming)
bullets: Core Pattern: 1D DP array dp[i] = min number of coins for amount i. Recurrence: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1).
Complexity: Time: O(Amount * Coins.length) | Space: O(Amount) array.
Edge Cases: Amount = 0 returns 0 | Unreachable amount returns -1 (initialized to infinity).

dsa_patterns.title: Trapping Rain Water (Two Pointers / Monotonic Stack)
bullets: Core Pattern: Two Pointers (left, right) with left_max and right_max trackers. If left_max < right_max, water trapped at left is left_max - height[left], move left inward.
Complexity: Time: O(N) single pass | Space: O(1) constant auxiliary memory.
Edge Cases: Strictly increasing/decreasing terrain traps 0 water | Less than 3 elevations.

dsa_patterns.title: Trie (Prefix Tree & Typeahead Search)
bullets: Core Pattern: Tree node with 26-child array / hash map + is_end boolean flag. Search/Insert iterates char by char.
Complexity: Insert: O(L) length of word | Search: O(L) | Prefix startsWith: O(L) | Space: O(Alphabet * N * L).
Edge Cases: Empty string search | Overlapping prefixes (app vs apple) | Unicode or special character sanitization.

dsa_patterns.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array (Modified Binary Search)
bullets: Core Pattern: Standard mid calculation. At least one half [low..mid] or [mid..high] is always strictly sorted. Check if target lies within sorted half to discard the other half.
Complexity: Time: O(log N) logarithmic steps | Space: O(1) iterative space.
Edge Cases: Target at exact pivot index | Array not rotated (fully sorted) | Array of length 1 or 2.

system_design_archetypes.title: Distributed Rate Limiter (Token Bucket / Redis Sliding Window)
bullets: Architecture: API Gateway -> Redis Cluster running atomic Lua scripts with Sliding Window Counter or Token Bucket.
Trade-offs: Token Bucket allows bursts with low memory; Sliding Window Counter gives smooth rate at cost of slight approximation.
Scale & Failure: Local in-memory fallback cache if Redis cluster degrades | Return HTTP 429 with 'Retry-After' header.

system_design_archetypes.title: URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bitly)
bullets: Architecture: Base62 encoding on 64-bit unique ID (Twitter Snowflake or Range-allocated DB counter) -> 7 chars yields 3.5 trillion URLs.
Storage & Cache: NoSQL / DynamoDB (Key: short_hash -> original_url) + Redis caching top 20% hot links with LRU eviction.
Redirect Logic: HTTP 301 (Permanent cacheable by browser) vs HTTP 302/307 (Temporary, enables real-time click analytics).

system_design_archetypes.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
bullets: Architecture: Hash ring [0, 2^32 - 1]. Both server nodes and keys are hashed onto the ring; key assigned to first node clockwise.
Virtual Nodes: Assign 100-250 virtual tokens per physical node to prevent hotspot skew and ensure uniform distribution.
Rebalancing: When node N joins or leaves, only K/N keys are migrated rather than entire database.

system_design_archetypes.title: Cache Invalidation, Stampede Protection & Patterns
bullets: Patterns: Cache-Aside (Lazy loading, app handles read/write) vs Write-Through (App writes to cache, cache writes to DB) vs Write-Behind.
Stampede / Thundering Herd: Protect hot key expiry via Mutex Lock (Singleflight coalescing) or Early Probabilistic Expiration (XFetch algorithm).
Penetration & Breakdown: Bloom Filter to reject non-existent IDs; Cache null values with short TTL for missing keys.

system_design_archetypes.title: Distributed Locks (Redis Redlock / ZooKeeper)
bullets: Redis Mechanism: `SET resource_name my_random_token NX PX 30000` (Atomic set if not exists with TTL) + Lua script to release only if token matches.
Redlock Multi-Node: Acquire lock on majority (N/2 + 1) independent Redis masters within timeout window to survive master node crashes.
Fencing Tokens: Monotonically increasing counter passed with every write to prevent split-brain zombies from overwriting newer transactions.

system_design_archetypes.title: Database Sharding & Horizontal Partitioning
bullets: Strategies: Hash-based sharding (uniform distribution, hard to range query) vs Range-based (great for timestamps, risk of hotspots) vs Directory-based.
Routing Tier: Stateless Shard Proxy (Vitess, Citus, or custom middleware) routing queries via Shard Key index map.
Pain Points & Mitigations: Avoid cross-shard joins by de-normalizing or co-locating related entity shards (e.g. users and user_orders on same shard).

system_design_archetypes.title: CAP Theorem & PACELC Trade-offs
bullets: CAP Core: Under Network Partition (P), you must choose either Consistency (C - reject stale writes) or Availability (A - serve stale data).
PACELC Extension: If Partition (P) -> choose Availability (A) or Consistency (C); Else (E) -> choose Latency (L) or Consistency (C).
Real-World Systems: Spanner/CockroachDB = CP; Cassandra/DynamoDB = AP (Tunable Quorum R + W > N for strong consistency).

system_design_archetypes.title: Distributed Transactions: 2PC vs Saga Pattern
bullets: Two-Phase Commit (2PC): Prepare phase (vote) -> Commit phase. Blocking protocol, vulnerable to coordinator failure and poor latency.
Saga Pattern: Sequence of local transactions coordinated via Events (Choreography) or Central Orchestrator. Each step has a compensating rollback action.
Idempotency Requirement: Every service endpoint must accept idempotency keys with unique UUIDs to safely retry without duplicate side effects.

system_design_archetypes.title: Real-Time Chat & Messaging (WhatsApp / Slack)
bullets: Connection Tier: Stateful WebSocket Gateway servers holding active TCP connections, coordinated by Redis Pub/Sub or Kafka.
Message Ingestion: Cassandra / ScyllaDB for write-heavy chat history (Partition Key: conversation_id, Clustering Key: message_timestamp).
Offline Delivery: Push Notification Service (APNs/FCM) triggered when recipient socket is disconnected.

system_design_archetypes.title: Kafka High-Throughput Event Streaming
bullets: Partitioning: Topics partitioned across brokers. Partition key hash ensures strict ordered delivery within each partition.
Zero-Copy Disk I/O: Sequential write to OS PageCache + `sendfile()` syscall bypasses user space directly to network socket.
Consumer Groups: Scaled horizontally up to partition count. Offset commits enable At-Least-Once or Exactly-Once via 2PC transactional producer.

system_design_archetypes.title: Database Storage Engines: B-Tree vs LSM Tree
bullets: B-Tree (PostgreSQL/MySQL): In-place balanced tree on disk. Fast O(log N) point lookups and range scans. Higher write amplification.
LSM-Tree (Cassandra/RocksDB): In-memory MemTable + Write-Ahead Log (WAL) flushed to immutable SSTables. Blazing write throughput; compaction merges SSTables.
Bloom Filters: Attached to each SSTable in LSM tree to immediately skip tables that do not contain the target key.

concurrency_os_networking.title: Deadlock Detection & Prevention (4 Coffman Conditions)
bullets: 4 Necessary Conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.
Prevention Strategies: Enforce global lock ordering (eliminates Circular Wait); use `tryLock()` with timeouts (eliminates No Preemption).
Detection & Recovery: Resource Allocation Graph with cycle detection -> Kill transaction with lowest rollback cost.

concurrency_os_networking.title: TCP vs UDP & Connection Lifecycle
bullets: TCP 3-Way Handshake: SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK. Provides reliable byte stream, flow control (sliding window), and congestion control (slow start).
UDP: Connectionless, zero handshake latency, no retransmissions. Ideal for real-time gaming, VoIP, DNS, and HTTP/3 (QUIC over UDP).
Termination: 4-way FIN/ACK handshake with TIME_WAIT state (2 * MSL) to ensure final ACK was received and drain duplicate packets.

concurrency_os_networking.title: SQL vs NoSQL Architectural Selection Matrix
bullets: Relational (PostgreSQL/MySQL): Strict ACID, complex relational joins, financial ledgers, transactional consistency, normalized schemas.
NoSQL (Mongo/Dynamo/Cassandra): High write volume, horizontal auto-sharding, unstructured/polymorphic payloads, high partition tolerance (BASE).
Polyglot Persistence: Combine PostgreSQL for core user/billing entities + Redis for ephemeral sessions + Cassandra for analytics logs.

concurrency_os_networking.title: Process vs Thread & Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)
bullets: Process vs Thread: Processes have isolated memory spaces; threads share heap/address space within the same process (fast context switch, race risk).
Python GIL: Mutex preventing multiple native threads from executing Python bytecodes simultaneously. Solves reference counting GC concurrency.
Bypassing GIL: Use `multiprocessing` for CPU-bound tasks (separate memory per core) or `asyncio` / thread pools for I/O-bound network calls.

behavioral_star_matrix.title: Major Production Outage & Root-Cause Resolution (STAR)
bullets: Situation & Task: Payment webhook processing latency spiked to 45s during peak flash sale, causing cascading timeout failures.
Action: Instated immediate circuit breaker, scaled Redis read-replicas, and optimized unindexed query causing table locks.
Result: Restored sub-50ms latency in 14 minutes; published blameless post-mortem and automated latency regression CI tests.

behavioral_star_matrix.title: Technical Architecture Disagreement & Consensus (STAR)
bullets: Situation & Task: Team was debating migrating monolithic auth service to gRPC microservices vs optimizing existing connection pooling.
Action: Built a benchmark spike proving 90% of latency was DB connection starvation, not HTTP/JSON overhead.
Result: Saved 3 months of refactor engineering time; deployed connection pool fix that reduced p99 latency by 68%.

behavioral_star_matrix.title: Tight Deadline & MVP Scope Negotiation (STAR)
bullets: Situation & Task: 4-week deadline for enterprise SSO integration with Fortune 500 client before quarter end.
Action: Decoupled custom directory sync into Phase 2; implemented standard SAML 2.0 / OIDC flow first with extensive automated smoke tests.
Result: Delivered 3 days ahead of schedule, secured $420k enterprise contract, and completed Phase 2 without technical debt.
